# Web Calculator Specification

## Overview

A browser-based calculator delivered as a static web application (HTML, CSS,
and vanilla JavaScript) requiring no build step or installation. It supports
basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), decimal
values, keyboard input, clear/backspace editing, and a persisted light/dark
theme, with a responsive layout usable on desktop, tablet, and mobile screens.

## Declared artifacts

index.html
css/styles.css
js/calculator.js
js/theme.js

## Acceptance criteria

Note: AC-012 is intentionally unassigned. No requirement or criterion was
dropped; the ID was reserved in an earlier draft and numbering resumes at
AC-013 so that previously assigned criterion IDs are preserved unchanged.

- AC-001: Opening index.html directly in a modern web browser (no build step, no server, no installation) loads a fully functional calculator.
- AC-002: The calculator UI displays ten number buttons labeled 0 through 9, each of which appends the corresponding digit to the current entry when selected.
- AC-003: Selecting the addition (+) operator followed by two operands and equals (=) computes and displays the correct sum.
- AC-004: Selecting the subtraction (-) operator followed by two operands and equals (=) computes and displays the correct difference.
- AC-005: Selecting the multiplication (×) operator followed by two operands and equals (=) computes and displays the correct product.
- AC-006: Selecting the division (÷) operator followed by two operands and equals (=) computes and displays the correct quotient.
- AC-007: A decimal point button allows entry of decimal values, and at most one decimal point is accepted per operand.
- AC-008: The current entry and calculation results are shown in a visible display area at all times during input and after evaluation.
- AC-009: Selecting the clear (C) control resets the display to 0 and discards any pending operand or operator.
- AC-010: Selecting the backspace/delete control removes the most recently entered character from the current entry without clearing the entire calculation.
- AC-011: Selecting the equals (=) button evaluates the current expression and displays the result in the display area.
- AC-013: Pressing number keys (0-9) on the keyboard enters digits identically to selecting the corresponding on-screen number button.
- AC-014: Pressing the +, -, *, and / keyboard keys applies the corresponding operator identically to selecting the corresponding on-screen operator button.
- AC-015: Pressing the Enter key evaluates the current expression identically to selecting the equals (=) button.
- AC-016: Pressing the Backspace key removes the most recently entered character identically to selecting the on-screen backspace control.
- AC-017: Pressing the Escape key clears the current calculation identically to selecting the on-screen clear (C) control.
- AC-018: A theme control lets the user switch between Light Mode and Dark Mode, immediately updating the visible appearance of the interface.
- AC-019: After selecting a theme and reloading the page or reopening the application in a new browser session, the previously selected theme is restored automatically.
- AC-020: The calculator layout renders without horizontal overflow or clipped controls at viewport widths from 320 pixels up through common desktop widths, including at typical tablet and mobile breakpoints.
- AC-021: Every calculator button exhibits a visibly distinct hover state and a visibly distinct keyboard-focus state compared to its resting state.
- AC-022: Display and button text maintain sufficient contrast against their background in both Light Mode and Dark Mode; the PRD does not specify a numeric contrast ratio, so the exact threshold is left as an open decision.
- AC-023: The application is fully usable without any login, sign-up, or authentication step.
- AC-024: The application loads and becomes usable within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
